full_judgment: 20.  It is already noted that the plaintiff got the suit fixed for peremptory hearing on 26-12 87 behind the back of the defendants upon filing an application on an off date although the defendants had been seriously contesting the suit by filing written statements. It is also seen that in the absence of the regular presiding judge of the court suit was disposed of ex parte by another Judge, who on that date was in-charge of the court and that the defendant's application for adjournment of hearing of the suit ex parte was not placed before the Judge concerned before hearing of the suit ex parte and even the said application is missing from the case record and that a manipulation in suit number in the daily cause list has been noted by the trial Court whereby TS No.142 of 1986 was shown as TS to 242 of 1986. It is clear from the materials on record that the defendants successfully proved in the trial Court the elements of fraud as alleged by them for setting aside the ex parte decree and that the plaintiff could not show that the ex parte disposal of the suit had been recorded in the daily cause list against Title Suit No. 142 of 1986 which could lead to a presumption of the defendant's knowledge of such ex parte disposal of the suit on 4-1-88. Thus, it appears that the learned Judges of the High Court Division did not at all consider the defendants against the plaintiff in upholding the gravity of allegations of fraud alleged by the judgment and order of the trial Court.
